chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan from Amr ibn Shamar from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
I asked him about the position of the two angels in the human being, so he said: 'One is here and one is here,' meaning at his two jawbones.

key_terms.الْمَلَكَيْنِ: The two angels (Kiraman Katibin) who record good and bad deeds
key_terms.شَدْقَيْهِ: His two jawbones/sides of the mouth

ai.seo_question: Where are the two recording angels located in the human body according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) specifies the anatomical location of the Kiraman Katibin as being situated at the sides of the jaw (shadqayn), linking the recording of deeds directly to the articulation of speech and the physical act of eating or speaking. This physical placement underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the tangible reality of divine observation, where the angels' proximity to the mouth highlights the significance of verbal conduct in the ledger of one's deeds.
